questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Haber process of production of ammonia $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is used as
questions.solution:
In the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia, finely divided iron is used as the catalyst.

To enhance the activity of the iron catalyst, small amounts of aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) and potassium oxide ($\text{K}_2\text{O}$) are added.

Substances that increase the efficiency or activity of a catalyst are known as promoters. Therefore, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ acts as a promoter.

Answer: Promoter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct decreasing order of bond dissociation enthalpy of halogens ?
questions.solution:
The bond dissociation enthalpy of halogens generally decreases down the group as the atomic size increases, which leads to less effective overlap of orbitals.

However, the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$ is exceptionally lower than that of $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$. This is due to the very small size of the fluorine atom, which results in strong interelectronic repulsions between the non-bonding electrons (lone pairs) on the two closely spaced fluorine atoms.

The experimental values of bond dissociation enthalpies are approximately:
$\text{Cl}_2 = 242.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{Br}_2 = 192.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{F}_2 = 158.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{I}_2 = 151.1 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Thus, the correct decreasing order of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$.

Answer: $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following oxoacids of chlorine exhibits $+3$ oxidation state of chlorine?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of chlorine be $x$.

In $\text{HClO}$:
$+1 + x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +1$

In $\text{HClO}_2$:
$+1 + x + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$

In $\text{HClO}_3$:
$+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5$

In $\text{HClO}_4$:
$+1 + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7$

Chlorine exhibits a $+3$ oxidation state in $\text{HClO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{HClO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of chlorine in its weakest oxoacid?
questions.solution:
The oxoacids of chlorine are $HClO$, $HClO_2$, $HClO_3$, and $HClO_4$.

The acidic strength of oxoacids of a halogen increases with an increase in the oxidation number of the halogen atom. As the number of oxygen atoms increases, the electron density is pulled away from the $O-H$ bond, making it easier to release an $H^+$ ion.

The order of acidic strength is $HClO < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4$.

Therefore, the weakest oxoacid of chlorine is hypochlorous acid, $HClO$.

Let the oxidation state of chlorine in $HClO$ be $x$.

The typical oxidation state of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$. Since the molecule is neutral, the sum of oxidation states is zero.

$(+1) + x + (-2) = 0$

$x - 1 = 0$

$x = +1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions exhibits the reducing property of ozone ?
questions.solution:
In the reaction $\text{NO}\text{(g)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, nitrogen is oxidized from $+2$ to $+4$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $2\text{KI}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{KOH}\text{(aq)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, iodine is oxidized from $-1$ to $0$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{PbS}\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, sulphur is oxidized from $-2$ to $+6$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, both hydrogen peroxide and ozone undergo mutual reduction. Ozone reduces $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and itself gets reduced to $\text{O}_2$. Thus, this reaction exhibits the reducing property of ozone.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$
questions.question: Which of the following reactions exhibits the reducing property of ozone ?
questions.explanation:
In the reaction $\text{NO}\text{(g)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, nitrogen is oxidized from $+2$ to $+4$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $2\text{KI}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{KOH}\text{(aq)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, iodine is oxidized from $-1$ to $0$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{PbS}\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)} + 4\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, sulphur is oxidized from $-2$ to $+6$. $\text{O}_3$ acts as an oxidizing agent.

In the reaction $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$, both hydrogen peroxide and ozone undergo mutual reduction. Ozone reduces $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and itself gets reduced to $\text{O}_2$. Thus, this reaction exhibits the reducing property of ozone.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(l)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following noble gases exhibits higher oxidation states ?
questions.solution:
As we move down the group of noble gases, the atomic size increases and the ionization enthalpy decreases.

Xenon has a relatively low ionization enthalpy, which allows its valence electrons to be excited to empty d-orbitals.

This enables Xenon to form compounds with highly electronegative elements like fluorine and oxygen.

Xenon exhibits higher oxidation states such as $+2$, $+4$, $+6$, and $+8$ in compounds like $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{XeF}_4$, $\text{XeF}_6$, $\text{XeO}_3$, and $\text{XeO}_4$.

Neon and Argon do not form stable compounds, and Krypton only forms $\text{KrF}_2$ with an oxidation state of $+2$.

Therefore, Xenon exhibits higher oxidation states.

Answer: Xe

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds has lowest thermal stability?
questions.solution:
The thermal stability of interhalogen compounds of the type $XY$ with respect to disproportionation follows the order:

$ClF > ICl > IBr > BrCl > BrF$

Bromine monofluoride (BrF$) is highly unstable and rapidly undergoes disproportionation at room temperature to form bromine trifluoride and bromine:

3BrF \rightarrow BrF_3 + Br_2$

Because of its high tendency to decompose, $BrF$ has the lowest thermal stability among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following catalysts is used in contact process of industrial production of sulfuric acid using $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ (air).
questions.solution:
The contact process is used for the industrial production of sulfuric acid.

The key step in this process is the catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) to sulfur trioxide ($\text{SO}_3$) using oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) from the air.

The reaction is:
$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$

This reaction is catalyzed by platinised asbestos or vanadium pentoxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$).

Among the given options, platinised asbestos is the correct catalyst.

Finely divided Ni is used in the hydrogenation of oils.
Co-Th is used in Fischer-Tropsch synthesis.
Fe-Cr is used in the Bosch process.

Answer: Platinised asbestos

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify weakest acid from following.
questions.solution:
The given acids are oxoacids of chlorine.

The chemical formulas and oxidation states of chlorine in these acids are:
Hypochlorous acid: $HClO$ (Oxidation state of $Cl = +1$)
Chlorous acid: $HClO_2$ (Oxidation state of $Cl = +3$)
Chloric acid: $HClO_3$ (Oxidation state of $Cl = +5$)
Perchloric acid: $HClO_4$ (Oxidation state of $Cl = +7$)

The acidic strength of oxoacids of the same halogen increases with an increase in the oxidation number of the halogen atom. This is because a higher oxidation state of the central atom leads to greater polarization of the $O-H$ bond, making it easier to release an $H^+$ ion. Alternatively, the stability of the conjugate base increases with the number of oxygen atoms due to greater resonance stabilization.

Thus, the order of acidic strength is $HClO < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4$.

Hypochlorous acid is the weakest acid among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is O-O bond length in ozone ?
questions.solution:
Ozone (O_3$) is a resonance hybrid of two equivalent structures.

Due to resonance, both O-O bonds in the ozone molecule are identical.

The O-O bond length is intermediate between a typical O-O single bond (148$ pm) and an O=O double bond (121$ pm).

The experimentally determined O-O bond length in ozone is 128$ pm.

Answer: $128$ pm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct decreasing order of oxidizing power of perhalate ions?
questions.solution:
The oxidizing power of perhalate ions depends on their standard reduction potentials. A higher positive standard reduction potential indicates a stronger oxidizing agent.

The standard reduction potentials ($E^{{}^{\circ}}$) for the reduction of perhalate ions to halate ions in acidic medium are:
$E^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{BrO}_4^- / \text{BrO}_3^-) = +1.74\text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{IO}_4^- / \text{IO}_3^-) = +1.65\text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{ClO}_4^- / \text{ClO}_3^-) = +1.20\text{ V}$

Since the reduction potential is highest for $\text{BrO}_4^-$ and lowest for $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the decreasing order of oxidizing power is $\text{BrO}_4^- > \text{IO}_4^- > \text{ClO}_4^-$.

The exceptionally high oxidizing power of $\text{BrO}_4^-$ is due to the relative instability of the $+7$ oxidation state of bromine, which arises from the poor shielding of the $3d$ electrons (d-block contraction or middle row anomaly).

Answer: $\text{BrO}_4^- > \text{IO}_4^- > \text{ClO}_4^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Charring process, concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with sugar to give sugar charcoal. What is the role of conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in this reaction?
questions.solution:
The reaction of concentrated sulfuric acid with sugar (sucrose) is known as the charring process.

$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} 12\text{C} + 11\text{H}_2\text{O}$

In this reaction, concentrated sulfuric acid removes water molecules from the sugar molecule, leaving behind a black mass of elemental carbon, which is called sugar charcoal. This demonstrates the strong affinity of concentrated sulfuric acid for water.

Therefore, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts as a strong dehydrating agent.

Answer: A dehydrating agent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the Xenon compounds in Column-1 with its structure in Column-II.
Column – IColumn – II
(a) $XeF_4$(i) pyramidal
(b) $XeF_6$(ii) square planar
(c) $XeOF_4$(iii) distorted octahedral
(d) $XeO_3$(iv) square pyramidal
questions.solution:
For $\text{XeF}_4$: Xenon has $8$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ single bonds with fluorine atoms and has $2$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar. Thus, (a) matches (ii).

For $\text{XeF}_6$: Xenon forms $6$ single bonds with fluorine atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3d^3$ and the shape is distorted octahedral. Thus, (b) matches (iii).

For $\text{XeOF}_4$: Xenon forms $4$ single bonds with fluorine atoms, $1$ double bond with oxygen, and has $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square pyramidal. Thus, (c) matches (iv).

For $\text{XeO}_3$: Xenon forms $3$ double bonds with oxygen atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is pyramidal. Thus, (d) matches (i).

The correct matching is (a) - (ii), (b) - (iii), (c) - (iv), (d) - (i).

Answer: (a) - (ii), (b) - (iii), (c) - (iv), (d) - (i)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not characteristics of interhalogen compounds?
options: Form addition products with unsaturated hydrocarbons.
questions.solution:
Interhalogen compounds are formed by the combination of two different halogens. They are covalent in nature due to the small electronegativity difference between the halogen atoms.

They are generally volatile solids or liquids (except $ClF$, which is a gas) and are not explosive.

They are highly reactive and form addition products with unsaturated hydrocarbons.

Because halogens are highly electronegative, interhalogen compounds have a strong tendency to accept electrons. Therefore, they act as strong oxidizing agents, not reducing agents.

Answer: Behave as strong reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following halogens does always show oxidation state -1 ?
questions.solution:
The oxidation state represents the number of electrons gained or lost when an atom forms chemical bonds. Halogens typically achieve a noble gas configuration by gaining one electron, resulting in a -1 oxidation state.

Fluorine consistently exhibits a -1 oxidation state due to its maximum electronegativity and absence of d-orbitals, preventing positive oxidation states.

Other halogens (chlorine, bromine, iodine) can display positive oxidation states (+1, +3, +5, +7) when bonded to more electronegative elements like oxygen, as their d-orbitals enable octet expansion in compounds such as $\mathrm{HClO4}$ or $\mathrm{ClF}_{3}$.

Thus, only fluorine always maintains an oxidation state of -1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is NOT acidic in nature?
questions.solution:
Oxides are classified as acidic, basic, amphoteric, or neutral. Non-metal oxides are typically acidic, though exceptions exist.

SO_{2} is an oxide of sulfur. It reacts with water to form sulfurous acid: $\mathrm{SO}_2(g) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

CO_{2} is an oxide of carbon. It reacts with water to form carbonic acid: $\mathrm{CO}_2(g) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

N_{2}O_{5} is an oxide of nitrogen. It reacts with water to form nitric acid: $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_5(s) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO}_3(aq)$, so it is acidic.

N_{2}O is also an oxide of nitrogen, but it is a neutral oxide and does not react with acids or bases, like CO and NO. Therefore, it is not acidic.

The oxide that is not acidic is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following xenon compound has chlorine pentafluoride like structure?
questions.solution:
Xenon compounds share structural similarities with interhalogens when their molecular geometries match. Chlorine pentafluoride (ClF_5$) has a square pyramidal geometry arising from an octahedral electron domain with one lone pair and five bonding pairs.

Among xenon compounds, XeF_4$ is square planar, XeF_6$ is distorted octahedral, and XeO_3$ is pyramidal. XeOF_4$ features xenon bonded to four fluorine atoms and one oxygen atom via a double bond, yielding five bonding domains and one lone pair. This $sp^3d^2$ hybridized configuration results in a square pyramidal geometry identical to $ClF_5$.

The xenon compound with structure analogous to $ClF_5$ is \boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is oxidation state of xenon in xenonmonooxytetrafluoride?
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of xenon in xenonmonooxytetrafluoride (XeOF_4$) is determined by considering the known oxidation states of oxygen and fluorine. Oxygen typically has an oxidation state of $-2$, and fluorine is always $-1$ in compounds. Since $XeOF_4$ is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states is zero.

Let $x$ be the oxidation state of xenon. The equation becomes:

$x + (-2) + 4(-1) = 0$

Simplifying: $x - 2 - 4 = 0$

Thus, $x - 6 = 0$ and $x = +6$.

The oxidation state of xenon is +6, corresponding to answer choice C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of oxygen atoms bonded to chlorine in its strongest oxoacid?
questions.solution:
The strongest oxoacid of chlorine is perchloric acid (HClO_4$), with chlorine as the central atom in a tetrahedral $sp^3$ hybridization.

The structure features one oxygen bonded to both chlorine and hydrogen ($-OH$ group) and three oxygen atoms double-bonded directly to chlorine.

Counting all oxygen atoms directly bonded to chlorine yields 1$ (from $-OH$) $+ 3$ (from $=O$) $= 4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about oxygen and sulphur?
options: Atoms of oxygen and sulphur consist two unpaired electrons in valence shell.
Oxygen and sulphur show $-2,+4$ and +6 oxidation states.
Oxygen is gas while sulphur is solid at room temperature.
Hydride of oxygen is more stable than hydride of sulphur.
questions.solution:
To identify the false statement, each option is evaluated against the chemical properties of oxygen and sulphur.

A) Both oxygen ($[\text{He}] 2s^2 2p^4$) and sulphur ($[\text{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^4$) possess two unpaired electrons in their valence p-orbitals. This statement is true.

B) Oxygen rarely exhibits oxidation states beyond $+2$ due to high electronegativity and lack of d-orbitals, whereas sulphur commonly shows $+4$ and $+6$ states. Oxygen does not demonstrate $+4$ or $+6$ oxidation states, making this statement false.

C) At room temperature, oxygen exists as a diatomic gas ($\text{O}_2$), and sulphur is a solid ($\text{S}_8$). This statement is true.

D) The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{O–H}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is greater than that of $\text{S–H}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, resulting in higher thermal stability for $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. This statement is true.

The false statement is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an acidic oxide?
questions.solution:
Oxide classification depends on the element's position in the periodic table and its oxidation state. Non-metal oxides are typically acidic while metal oxides are basic, though exceptions exist such as neutral oxides.

Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), and nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$) are all neutral oxides that do not react with acids or bases.

Dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) is acidic, reacting with water to form nitric acid: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HNO}_3$. It also forms salts with bases.

Thus, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is the acidic oxide among the options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is existing oxoacid of fluorine?
questions.solution:
The only known oxoacid of fluorine is hypofluorous acid, HOF. Due to fluorine's extreme electronegativity, it cannot exhibit positive oxidation states in oxoacids like other halogens. In HOF, fluorine maintains its typical $-1$ oxidation state, hydrogen is $+1$, and oxygen is $0$.

For other compounds such as $\mathrm{HFO}_2$, $\mathrm{HFO}_3$, and $\mathrm{HFO}_4$, fluorine would need to adopt positive oxidation states ($+3$, $+5$, and $+7$ respectively), which contradicts its chemical behavior.

Thus, the correct option is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following interhalogen compounds in liquid state at room temperature?
questions.solution:
Liquid interhalogen compounds at room temperature (20–25°C) are identified by comparing their phase transition temperatures:

$\text{ICl}$ exists as a red-brown liquid, with the beta form melting at $13.9°\text{C}$ and boiling at $97°\text{C}$.

$\text{BrF}_5$ melts at $-60°\text{C}$ and boils at $40.3°\text{C}$, remaining liquid within the room temperature range.

$\text{ClF}_3$ boils at $11.75°\text{C}$ and $\text{IF}_7$ sublimes at $4.77°\text{C}$, both being gaseous under these conditions.

Thus, only $\text{ICl}$ and $\text{BrF}_5$ are liquids at room temperature.

$\boxed{\text{A, C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is shape of interhalogen compound so that central halogen exhibits +3 oxidation state?
questions.solution:
Consider $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ where chlorine exhibits a +3 oxidation state. Fluorine's -1 oxidation state gives a total of -3, balanced by chlorine's +3 state.

Chlorine has 7 valence electrons. Bonding with three fluorine atoms uses 3 electrons, leaving 4 electrons that form 2 lone pairs. The total electron pairs are 5, resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry.

Lone pairs occupy equatorial positions to minimize repulsion, forcing the three bonding pairs into a T-shaped molecular geometry.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following inert gases is used for magnetic resonance imaging?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A) He.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machines utilize powerful superconducting magnets that require cooling to approximately 4 Kelvin to maintain their superconducting state. Liquid helium serves as the optimal cryogenic coolant due to its exceptionally low boiling point of 4.2 K at atmospheric pressure, which is capable of achieving these ultra-low temperatures. Its inert nature prevents chemical reactions with MRI components.

Other inert gases—neon, argon, and xenon—have significantly higher boiling points and cannot reach the necessary temperature range for superconducting magnet operation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following compounds that valence shell of 'Xe' consists one lone pair of electrons.
questions.solution:
Valence shell electron counting determines lone pairs on xenon. Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Each single bond contributes 1 electron to bonding, while double bonds contribute 2.

For D) $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$, the bonding electron count is $4 \times 1 + 1 \times 2 = 6$. Non-bonding electrons are $8 - 6 = 2$, forming $2 / 2 = 1$ lone pair.

The central Xe atom in $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$ contains exactly one lone pair.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the molecular formula of halous acid of chlorine?
questions.solution:
The oxyacids of chlorine include hypochlorous acid $\mathrm{HClO}$, chlorous acid $\mathrm{HClO}_2$ (also known as halous acid), chloric acid $\mathrm{HClO}_3$, and perchloric acid $\mathrm{HClO}_4$.

Halous acid corresponds specifically to chlorous acid, whose molecular formula is $\mathrm{HClO}_2$.

Final answer: B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following halogen forms maximum number of oxoacids?
questions.solution:
The formation of oxoacids by halogens depends on the availability of d-orbitals to expand the octet, allowing multiple oxidation states.

Fluorine cannot expand its octet and forms only one oxoacid: hypofluorous acid $\mathrm{HOF}$ (oxidation state $+1$).

Chlorine, with available d-orbitals, forms four stable oxoacids: hypochlorous $\mathrm{HClO}$ ($+1$), chlorous $\mathrm{HClO_2}$ ($+3$), chloric $\mathrm{HClO_3}$ ($+5$), and perchloric acid $\mathrm{HClO_4}$ ($+7$).

Bromine forms hypobromous $\mathrm{HBrO}$ ($+1$), bromic $\mathrm{HBrO_3}$ ($+5$), and perbromic acid $\mathrm{HBrO_4}$ ($+7$), omitting the unstable bromous acid $\mathrm{HBrO_2}$ ($+3$).

Iodine forms hypoiodous $\mathrm{HIO}$ ($+1$), iodic $\mathrm{HIO_3}$ ($+5$), and periodic acid $\mathrm{HIO_4}$ or $\mathrm{H_5IO_6}$ ($+7$), excluding the unstable iodous acid $\mathrm{HIO_2}$ ($+3$).

Chlorine forms the maximum number of stable oxoacids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the different types of bonds formed by sulphur with oxygen in thiosulfuric acid?
options: One double bond and two single bond
One double bond and one single bond
Two double bond and one single bond
Two double bond and two single bond
questions.solution:
The molecular structure of thiosulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$) features a central sulfur atom bonded to three oxygen atoms and one terminal sulfur atom. This sulfur-oxygen bonding consists of one $\text{S}=\text{O}$ double bond and two $\text{S}-\text{O}$ single bonds.

$\text{HO}-\text{S}-\text{OH}|\text{S}=\text{O}$

The central sulfur thus forms one double bond and two single bonds with oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about interhalogen compounds?
options: They are more reactive than halogens.
If these are represented as $\mathrm{XX}^1$, number of $\mathrm{X}^1$ atoms is always even.
questions.solution:
Interhalogen compounds ($\mathrm{XX'_n}$) are covalent and diamagnetic due to paired electrons. They demonstrate greater reactivity than elemental halogens because their polar bonds are more susceptible to attack.

The general formula permits $n$ values of 1, 3, 5, or 7, all odd. Since the statement claims the number of $\mathrm{X'}$ atoms is always even, it is false.

$\boxed{\mathrm{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct decreasing order of boiling point for hydrides of halogens.
questions.solution:
The boiling points of hydrogen halides are determined by their intermolecular forces.

Hydrogen fluoride (HF) exhibits strong hydrogen bonding due to fluorine's high electronegativity and small size, resulting in a significantly elevated boiling point compared to other hydrogen halides.

Hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen bromide (HBr), and hydrogen iodide (HI) lack hydrogen bonding capabilities. Their boiling points depend on London dispersion forces, which strengthen with increasing molecular size and electron count.

$\text{HI} > \text{HBr} > \text{HCl}$ due to HI's largest molecular size and highest electron count, producing the strongest London dispersion forces. HBr exhibits intermediate strength, while HCl has the weakest forces.

HF's hydrogen bonding gives it the highest boiling point, exceeding even HI's. The complete ordering is $\text{HF} > \text{HI} > \text{HBr} > \text{HCl}$.

This corresponds to option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify false statement from the following about fluorine.
options: It has high bond dissociation enthalpy among all halogens.
questions.solution:
Analysis of statements about fluorine:

Fluorine is the most electronegative element (Pauling scale 3.98), confirming statement A is true.

Due to its extreme electronegativity, fluorine cannot exhibit positive oxidation states and maintains only a -1 oxidation state, making statement B true.

The order of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\text{Cl}_2$ (242 kJ/mol) $ > \text{Br}_2$ (193 kJ/mol) $ > \text{F}_2$ (158 kJ/mol) $ > \text{I}_2$ (151 kJ/mol). Interelectronic repulsions between lone pairs in $\text{F}_2$ weaken its bond, making it lower than chlorine and bromine. Statement C is false.

Fluorine forms only hypofluorous acid (HOF) as its oxoacid, lacking d-orbitals for octet expansion, confirming statement D is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following set of elements is present in apatite ?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct order of thermal stability of hydrides of 16 group elements from the following.
questions.solution:
The thermal stability of Group 16 element hydrides is determined by the E–H bond strength, where E represents the central atom.

Bond strength decreases down the group due to increasing atomic size, which lengthens the bond and lowers the bond dissociation enthalpy. Weaker bonds dissociate more readily, reducing thermal stability.

The Group 16 elements in order of increasing atomic size are O < S < Se < Te, leading to the order of increasing E–H bond length: H–O < H–S < H–Se < H–Te. Consequently, bond strength decreases: H–O > H–S > H–Se > H–Te, and thermal stability follows the same decreasing order: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te}$.

Expressed in increasing thermal stability: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Comparing with the options, only C matches this order: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.q: Which mixture is used for respiration by deep sea divers?
questions.solution: $Scuba divers must cope with high concentrations of dissolved gases while breathing air at high pressure, underwater. Increased pressure increases the solubility of atmospheric gases in blood. When divers come towards surface, the pressure gradually decreases. This called bends.
